title: Knowledge sovereignty holds across supported observable surfaces
claim: For protected ontology, operational and provenance knowledge, principals with identical low-authority views cannot distinguish worlds that differ only in data outside their disclosure authority through supported queries, tools, errors, subscriptions, identifiers or provenance surfaces.
null_hypothesis: Write authorization can be strong while the system still leaks protected knowledge through query shape, object existence, error messages, generated tools, subscriptions or provenance relationships.
rivals: Field/row-level authorization in a conventional API gives the same non-disclosure property without ontology semantics.
Perfect noninterference is impractical; the candidate will need undocumented exceptions that make the claim unfalsifiable.
The test only proves direct read denial and misses inference through existence or relationship structure.
mechanism: Read/disclosure capability is derived from the same versioned authority contract as Actions; generated surfaces omit unauthorized capabilities and the runtime applies uniform redaction/nonexistence semantics over objects, links, provenance and subscriptions.
scope: Supported application-layer surfaces only: object/query/function/tool schemas, errors, subscriptions/events and provenance APIs. Hardware, network-traffic analysis, model memorization and micro-timing side channels are explicitly excluded.
predictions: World pairs differing only in inaccessible protected facts produce identical low-observable outputs for an unauthorized principal.
Unauthorized object or link existence cannot be learned through identifier probing where the disclosure contract says existence is secret.
Generated tools and schemas do not reveal hidden resource/action metadata beyond the principal capability set.
Provenance queries redact protected actors/evidence/links without corrupting the authorized portion of the chain.
falsifiers: Any protected fact, existence bit or relationship is distinguishable through a frozen supported low-observable channel without disclosure authority.
A generated schema/tool reveals a hidden capability or protected structural metadata.
Redaction makes authorized provenance semantically false rather than explicitly partial/redacted.

experiment.summary: Differential noninterference experiment over paired worlds that differ only in inaccessible secrets, plus direct exfiltration fuzzing.
steps: Freeze disclosure labels, principals, protected facts and the set of low-observable application channels.
Generate paired worlds equal on authorized facts and different on protected facts.
Execute the same query/tool/error/subscription/provenance observations in each world.
Compare canonicalized low outputs and classify any difference against explicit allowed-disclosure rules.
Inject existence-leak, error-detail, hidden-tool and provenance-link mutants.

oracle: Frozen disclosure lattice plus a canonical low-observation projection that is independent of candidate query/tool implementation.
baseline: Conventional typed service with row/field-level authorization and response/schema redaction under the same disclosure lattice.

support_if: 0 unauthorized low-observable divergences across at least 5,000 paired worlds.
0 hidden capability/schema disclosures outside the frozen lattice.
0 false provenance statements introduced by redaction.
reject_if: Any frozen supported channel leaks a protected fact/existence/relationship or hidden capability outside disclosure authority.
inconclusive_if: Paired-world corpus omits object/link/provenance/tool-discovery cases or protected facts are not actually varied.
invalid_if: The candidate controls the canonicalization oracle, or post-reveal exclusions remove a leaking supported channel without a new freeze.

python_hypothesis_role.strategy: Generate paired worlds, principals, disclosure labels, graph relationships and observation sequences; shrink any distinguishing protected fact/channel pair.
python_hypothesis_role.mutation_proof: Return 403 vs 404 for secret existence, leak a hidden tool schema, and retain a protected provenance edge; all must be detected.

stop_conditions: If practical disclosure requires a weaker property than application-layer noninterference, reject this claim and preregister the weaker leakage budget explicitly.
